evals.name: founder-profile-audit
evals.prompt: LinkedIn strategy for our CEO (B2B cybersecurity, 2,900 followers). Last 90 days: 14 posts — 9 were links to our blog (avg 1,100 impressions, 6 reactions), 3 text posts about incidents she handled (avg 7,800 impressions, 60 reactions, 14 comments), 2 company reposts. Headline: 'CEO at ShieldOps'. She has 2 hours/week. Goal: inbound demo requests from CISOs.
evals.expected_output: Audit in the skill's format: link posts diagnosed as the reach problem, text/story posts as the winner, headline rewrite with audience and outcome, 4–5 pillars, a 2-hours-a-week cadence (2–3 posts + commenting), comment flywheel targets by type, Featured section with a demo link, personal vs company page roles.
assertions: Identifies link posts (9 of 14) as the main reach drag and the incident text posts as the format to scale
Rewrites the headline from a job title to who she helps + outcome + proof
Cadence fits 2 hours/week (e.g. 2–3 posts and 15–20 min commenting on 2–3 days) rather than daily posting
Includes a comment flywheel with target account types (CISOs, security communities)
Does not recommend the retired Creator Mode toggle; mentions setting Follow as primary button if relevant

evals.name: company-page-vs-personal
evals.prompt: Our marketing team posts 5x a week on our company page (4,000 followers) and gets ~300 impressions per post. The founders don't post. Leadership wants to double down on the page with a bigger budget for design. Is that the right move?
evals.expected_output: Explains structural reach limits of company pages, recommends a people-first approach (founders/employees post, page amplifies), gives a practical employee advocacy process, and what the page should still do.
assertions: Explains that company pages have structurally lower reach than personal profiles and that more design budget won't fix distribution
Recommends founders/employees posting with the page amplifying, including an advocacy process
Keeps a role for the page (credibility hub, official news, complete profile)
Provides a measurable plan (what to post where, KPIs)

evals.name: post-rewrite-for-reach
evals.prompt: Rewrite this LinkedIn post so it actually gets reach: 'Excited to share our new whitepaper on supply chain resilience! Download here: https://acme.com/whitepaper #supplychain #logistics #resilience #innovation #leadership Please like and share!'
evals.expected_output: A rewritten text post with a strong first line, one concrete insight from the whitepaper (or a placeholder), no link in the body (link in first comment), no engagement bait, 0–3 hashtags, and a closing question; plus a short explanation of each change.
assertions: Removes the external link from the body and puts it in the first comment
Removes 'Please like and share' and the hashtag pile (keeps 0–3)
First line carries a specific idea or tension rather than 'Excited to share'
Explains the reasoning for each change briefly
